title: Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI
exclusions: Does not replace enterprise SIEM correlation for unrelated threat classes. Does not constitute legal, regulatory, or executive attestation for 'Splunk SOAR + ISE Closed-Loop Playbook Audit and Mean-Time-to-Containment KPI'. Does not cover entities explicitly scoped out in operational_exceptions.csv. Pair with sibling UCs in the same subcategory when the SPL surface alone cannot prove control effectiveness (see prerequisiteUseCases on UC-17.1.82).
evidence: Saved search uc_17_1_82_splunk_soar_ise_closed_loop_playbook_aud, dashboard panel tied to this UC, weekly CSV export archived to index=evidence with change-ticket reference, and git-tracked lookup baselines referenced in the search.

compliance.controlObjective: Mean-time-to-contain KPI for ANC-driven SOAR playbook executions.

compliance.assurance_rationale: DORA Art.17 ICT-related incident management — automated containment efficacy.
SOC-2 CC7.4 incident response — automated containment.

controlTest.positiveScenario: Run a SOAR `block_endpoint` playbook. Confirm ISE 86001 ANC apply within 30s.
controlTest.negativeScenario: All playbooks succeed within target MTTC. No fire.

dataSources: Splunk SOAR audit logs `index=phantom` showing playbook runs, action results from the *Cisco ISE* SOAR app (https://splunkbase.splunk.com/app/4250) — `block_endpoint`, `unblock_endpoint`, `endpoint_session_info` actions. Combine with ISE syslog 86001 (ANC-applied) to audit reach.
app: `Splunk SOAR Cisco ISE App` (Splunkbase 4250) + Splunk SOAR.
spl:
index=phantom action_name=block_endpoint
| eval soar_apply_time=_time
| stats earliest(soar_apply_time) as soar_t, latest(_time) as last_action by container_id, mac_address
| join mac_address [search index=nac sourcetype="cisco:ise:syslog" MessageCode=86001 anc_action=quarantine | rename _time as ise_apply_time]
| eval soar_to_ise_lag_s=ise_apply_time - soar_t
| stats avg(soar_to_ise_lag_s) as avg_lag, max(soar_to_ise_lag_s) as max_lag
description: Audits Splunk SOAR playbook → ISE ANC closed-loop performance. Measures (a) SOAR `block_endpoint` action success rate, (b) average lag from SOAR action to ISE 86001 confirmation, and (c) max lag (worst case).
value: Automated containment is only as fast as its slowest link. SOAR playbook audit gives the SOC measurable evidence that playbooks executed end-to-end, satisfying NIS2/DORA incident-response requirements with quantitative MTTC.
implementation: Schedule the search every 1 hour over the last 24 hours; emit MTTC KPI to a summary index for the SOAR-effectiveness dashboard.
visualization: MTTC trend; per-playbook success rate; failed-action log.
knownFalsePositives:
1. **Scheduled maintenance windows** — Planned change activity in the CMDB or change calendar produces expected deviations that match this detection pattern during approved maintenance. Cross-check ServiceNow change records for `state=implement` and the affected CI list.

2. **Backup and batch job cycles** — Nightly ETL, backup agents, or log rotation jobs generate bursts of similar events that resemble alert conditions but occur on a fixed schedule. Compare `_time` against the documented batch window before paging.

3. **Onboarding and provisioning bursts** — New users, devices, or services provisioned in bulk can temporarily skew counts until baselines stabilize. Filter events tagged `onboarding=true` in the identity or asset lookup.

4. **Monitoring and health-check traffic** — Synthetic transactions or internal scanner accounts generate probe traffic designed to exercise the control. Exclude service accounts listed in `monitoring_exceptions.csv`.

**Suppression mechanism:** Maintain a KV Store lookup `operational_exceptions.csv` with columns `entity`, `exception_reason`, `valid_from`, `valid_until`, and `approved_by`. Join the saved search to this lookup and filter `where isnull(exception_reason) OR now() > valid_until` so approved windows suppress alerts without muting the search globally.
mitreAttack: N/A (meta-detection — measures playbook execution KPIs, not adversary behaviour)
detailedImplementation:
Standard pattern.

Step 1 — Configure data collection

Install and configure the add-on referenced in the app field (`Splunk SOAR Cisco ISE App` (Splunkbase 4250) + Splunk SOAR.). Enable the modular input or HEC token that writes sourcetype=cisco:ise:syslog into phantom, nac. Default poll interval 300–900 seconds unless the vendor API rate-limits lower. Grant the ingestion role `list_inputs` and `search` on the target index.

Step 2 — Create the search and alert

Schedule the SPL with earliest=-24h@h and throttle per entity to avoid duplicate pages. Document tunable macros in the comment header. Understanding this SPL: filters in the first pipeline reduce license cost; stats/timechart aggregates define the alert grain; joins/lookups enrich owner or asset metadata for routing.

Step 3 — Validate

Compare `| tstats count where index=... sourcetype=...` against the vendor admin UI inventory count (+/-5%). Spot-check two known entities for field presence (`container_id, mac_address`). Run `timechart count span=1h` over 7 days to find ingestion gaps longer than two poll intervals.

Step 4 — Operationalize

Add a dashboard row with single-value KPI tiles, a 24-hour timechart, and a drilldown table mirroring the SPL output columns. Route critical severity to the platform on-call channel; route warning to the service owner from the lookup.

Step 5 — Troubleshooting

No events: verify forwarder connectivity, HEC token ACLs, and that the modular input appears in `index=_internal source=*splunkd*`. NULL fields: check props/transforms order and TA version. Fewer results than expected: confirm index allow-lists on the search head role and that `_time` uses the correct timezone. API errors: inspect splunkd.log for HTTP 401/429 from the vendor endpoint configured in inputs.conf.
grandmaExplanation: Splunk SOAR is the automation that runs playbooks. When SOAR tells ISE to quarantine a device, we measure how long it takes — and prove the response actually happened.
